# COSMOS — Beyond the Horizon

> An interactive 3D solar system simulation and astronomy exploration platform built with React, Three.js, and authentic NASA/JPL telemetry.

Website: https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk
Source Repository: https://github.com/sushenjayasuriya/cosmos-explorer
Attribution: NASA, JPL-Caltech, ESA, STScI, ESO

## Platform Overview

COSMOS transforms solar system observation into an educational platform spanning planetary science, deep-space missions, astrophysics, and space imaging.

### Core Sections

- [Solar System Explorer](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/): Real-time interactive 3D planetary simulation featuring the Sun, 8 planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), 7 moons (The Moon, Io, Europa, Ganymede, Titan, Enceladus, Triton), and planetary telemetry.
- [Space Missions Explorer](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions): Comprehensive catalog and interactive 3D models of humanity's landmark robotic spacecraft.
- [Astronomy Encyclopedia](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover): Researched educational articles on stellar evolution, black holes, galactic dynamics, exoplanets, and space technology.
- [Deep Space Gallery](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/gallery): High-resolution imagery from Hubble, JWST, Chandra, and NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) video observations.

## Landmark Space Missions

- [Voyager 1](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/voyager-1): Launched 1977 by NASA. First human-made object to enter interstellar space (>24 billion km from Earth). Explored Jupiter and Saturn. Carries the Golden Record.
- [Voyager 2](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/voyager-2): Launched 1977 by NASA. The only probe to explore all four giant outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) and now in interstellar space.
- [Cassini-Huygens](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/cassini-huygens): Launched 1997 by NASA/ESA/ASI. Orbited Saturn for 13 years; discovered water-ice plumes on Enceladus and deployed the Huygens probe onto Titan's hydrocarbon surface.
- [Juno](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/juno): Launched 2011 by NASA. Solar-powered polar orbiter investigating Jupiter's deep atmosphere, magnetic dynamo, and core composition.
- [Mars 2020 Perseverance](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/perseverance): Launched 2020 by NASA. Rover searching for ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater, producing oxygen with MOXIE, and deploying the Ingenuity helicopter.
- [New Horizons](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/new-horizons): Launched 2006 by NASA. High-speed flyby of Pluto and Charon in 2015, followed by Kuiper Belt planetesimal Arrokoth in 2019.
- [Europa Clipper](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/europa-clipper): Launched October 2024 by NASA. En route to Jupiter to assess the habitability of Europa's subsurface liquid ocean.
- [James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/missions/jwst): Launched 2021 by NASA/ESA/CSA. Premier infrared space observatory stationed at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2), observing first-generation stars and exoplanetary atmospheres.

## Researched Astronomy Articles

- [How Stars Are Born](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/how-stars-are-born): Gravitational collapse of molecular gas clouds, Jeans mass, and protostellar ignition.
- [The Life Cycle of a Star](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/the-life-cycle-of-a-star): Main sequence equilibrium, red giant expansion, planetary nebulae, white dwarfs, neutron stars, and core-collapse supernovae.
- [What Is a Black Hole?](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/what-is-a-black-hole): General relativity spacetime curvature, singularities, and stellar-mass vs. supermassive black holes.
- [Event Horizons Explained](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/event-horizons-explained): Schwarzschild radius, light trapping boundaries, gravitational time dilation, and photon spheres.
- [The Milky Way Galaxy](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/the-milky-way-galaxy): Barred spiral structure, Sagittarius A* central black hole, stellar populations, and dark matter halo.
- [Andromeda Galaxy](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/andromeda-galaxy): Messier 31 characteristics, local group dynamics, and future Milky Way collision trajectory.
- [Types of Galaxies](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/types-of-galaxies): Hubble classification scheme: spirals, ellipticals, lenticulars, and irregulars.
- [What Are Nebulae?](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/what-are-nebulae): Interstellar clouds of dust, hydrogen, and helium; emission, reflection, dark, and planetary nebulae.
- [The Pillars of Creation](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/the-pillars-of-creation): Eagle Nebula (M16) star-forming towers observed in optical and infrared by Hubble and JWST.
- [How Exoplanets Are Discovered](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/how-exoplanets-are-discovered): Transit photometry (Kepler, TESS), radial velocity Doppler shifts, gravitational microlensing, and direct imaging.
- [Habitable Zones](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/habitable-zones): Circumstellar Goldilocks zones, liquid water equilibrium, stellar irradiance, and planetary atmospheres.
- [The Kuiper Belt](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/the-kuiper-belt): Trans-Neptunian disc of icy planetesimals, dwarf planets (Pluto, Haumea, Makemake), and resonant orbits.
- [The Oort Cloud](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/the-oort-cloud): Hypothetical spherical reservoir of billions of icy cometary nuclei extending up to 100,000 AU.
- [How Spacecraft Navigate](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/how-spacecraft-navigate): Deep Space Network (DSN) radiometric tracking, celestial optical star trackers, and gravity-assist slingshots.
- [How the James Webb Space Telescope Works](https://cosmos.sushenjayasuriya.org.lk/discover/how-the-james-webb-space-telescope-works): Beryllium hexagonal mirror optics, five-layer Kapton sunshield, cryogenic cooling, and infrared instruments (NIRCam, MIRI, NIRSpec, NIRISS).
